paragraphs: Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians (the U.S. counterpart is BLS/O*NET 49-3011 aircraft mechanics and service technicians and 49-2091 avionics technicians) diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft engines, airframe structures and onboard systems, and complete inspections and release sign-offs as required. The workplace is a hangar, a maintenance station or the apron, and the core measures are airworthiness, maintenance to the manual and traceable records, not flight operations or airline operations. People worth exploring this usually want to work step by step to the manual and the job card, judge faults with instruments and measuring tools, and are prepared for airworthiness responsibility and a noisy environment.

Three short self-test tasks: from public material put together a landing-gear inspection job card that includes the steps, the tools and the inspection points; complete one component measurement record using fictional figures (with the readings, the tolerance and the verdict); and write up one troubleshooting exercise as a record containing the symptom, the hypothesis, the test, the conclusion and the release judgement. Doing them incompletely is normal; the point is to observe your own real reaction to working step by step to the manual, to precision requirements and to leaving a documented trail. (Editorial suggestion, not a hiring or licence test.)

People more likely to adapt: those who can work step by step to the manual and the job card without skipping steps, who are willing to re-check with instruments and measuring tools, who can accept noise, temperature and contaminant environments and wear protective equipment as required, and who respect airworthiness and sign-off responsibility. The risk is usually greater for those unwilling to follow the manual, inclined to bypass inspection points on experience, or uncomfortable with precise records and responsible sign-off.

The U.S. wages and employment on this page come from the same BLS basis shown by the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook and O*NET: 49-3011 aircraft mechanics and service technicians, a median annual wage of 79,870 U.S. dollars in 2025, month 5 (May); the combined group (49-3011 and 49-2091) had about 159,800 people employed in 2025, growth of 6% over 2025—2035 and about 13,100 openings a year; the 49-3011 employment shown by O*NET is about 139,400 people in 2024, growth of 4% over 2024—2034 and on average about 11,300 job openings a year across the projection period. The two bases and periods differ, and each item is labelled on this page. Mainland China has no precise national wage distribution for this occupation, so the industry-category and unit-type figures serve only as a broad-basis reference; the maintenance personnel licence, type ratings and release authority follow the Rules on the Administration of Licences for Civil Aircraft Maintenance Personnel and the employer's own rules, and this page is not a legal opinion.

In one sentence: a technical post that diagnoses, repairs or overhauls aircraft airframes, engines and onboard systems in a hangar, a maintenance station or the apron under continuing airworthiness documents, carries out inspections and signs off a maintenance release within the authority granted.

The tasks of aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians fall into four groups: inspection and diagnosis (inspect airframes, landing gear, hydraulic and de-icing systems to the job card and the manual, locate cracks, distortion and wear with X-rays, magnetic-particle testing and precision measuring tools, and listen to a running engine to judge a fault); repair and overhaul (replace or repair worn, defective or damaged parts, remove and install engines and components, and adjust and overhaul to the manual); inspection and release (check whether completed work meets the standards and the continuing airworthiness documents, carry out routine and special inspections as required, and sign off the release within the authority granted); and records and reporting (maintain the maintenance log, record preventive and corrective maintenance, and report a defect or unairworthy condition as required).

O*NET 49-3011.00 aircraft mechanics and service technicians: diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft engines and components such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems. Common job titles include airframe and powerplant mechanic (A&P), aviation maintenance technician (AMT), helicopter mechanic and aircraft mechanic. Following the BLS combined basis, this page also covers 49-2091 avionics technicians (install, test, adjust and repair aircraft electronic systems).

China's CCAR-66-R3 application conditions are checked under Article 66.6 for age, colour vision, a college diploma, basic-knowledge training, maintenance experience or qualifying practical training, the licence examination and completion of the technical English level test. The English test is completed and graded, and no uniform pass threshold may be invented; releasing a complex aircraft additionally requires the corresponding type rating, while non-complex aircraft and component authority are checked separately.

Keep the job card, the measurement readings, the torque values, the replaced parts and the inspection sign-off records, so that a maintenance or release decision can be traced back to the specific job card, component and authorised person.

The boundary comes down to four things: who sets the repair plan and the release standard, who carries out the maintenance and the inspection, who flies the aircraft, and who is responsible for operations and airworthiness oversight. Maintenance technicians carry out maintenance and inspection to the manual and the continuing airworthiness documents and sign off the release within the authority granted; flight operations are the pilot's responsibility; the repair plan and the release standard are set by the continuing airworthiness documents and the civil aviation authority; airworthiness oversight rests with the civil aviation authority; and a modification or design change beyond the authority granted must go through the airworthiness certification procedure.
Carry out maintenance to the manual and the job card, and sign off the release within the authority granted.
Answer airworthiness and responsibility questions with 'which manual, what inspection was done, what value was measured, and who released it'.

The core of this occupation is the maintenance, inspection and recording of aircraft and onboard equipment; some avionics tasks can also involve modification design, and particular individuals may additionally hold authorised inspection or certification duties. The specific qualifications and approval authority must be checked against the jurisdiction and the real post documents, and are not uniformly excluded by the occupation title.

The object is the aircraft airframe, engine, propeller and onboard systems; the basis is the continuing airworthiness documents, the maintenance manual, the job card, and the licence with its type ratings.

Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians (the U.S. counterpart is BLS/O*NET 49-3011 aircraft mechanics and service technicians and 49-2091 avionics technicians) diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft airframes, engines and onboard systems: inspect to the job card and the manual with non-destructive testing, replace or repair parts, test and adjust systems, complete inspections and sign off a maintenance release within the authority granted, and keep traceable maintenance records. The workplace is a hangar, a maintenance station or the apron. On the mainland China side, civil aircraft maintenance personnel are under a licence system, the licence is issued uniformly by the Civil Aviation Administration of China, is classified by aeroplane and rotorcraft and states the engine category, and releasing a complex aircraft requires an added type rating. As a boundary, this is not the same as a pilot who flies the aircraft, nor the same as a regulatory post that sets airworthiness standards or performs airworthiness certification.

Digital job cards and test records can help keep the trail; the actual maintenance, inspection and release authority is checked against the jurisdiction, the aircraft or component and the post authorisation, and a tool cannot obtain or replace the required qualifications.
Receive the job card and the manual → inspection and diagnosis → decide the repair plan → work to the manual → inspect and sign off the release → record and report.
Output is measured by airworthiness status, compliance with the standard and traceable records, not by completion speed alone.
Maintenance job cards and inspection records, measurement readings and torque records, replaced-part registers, defect and unairworthy-condition reports, and release sign-off documents.
Work is divided by aircraft type and system, and before starting you should check the licence category, the type ratings and the scope of the authority.

Maintenance, inspection and release are each checked against the jurisdiction and the specific authority. The U.S. BLS distinguishes approved courses, on-the-job training and military training; an approved course can substitute for part of the examination eligibility and experience requirement, and an uncertificated person may perform maintenance under the supervision of a certificated A&P holder. Avionics posts may carry employer certification and similar requirements, and A&P or a course must not be generalised into a threshold for every post. In China, releasing a complex aircraft requires the licence and the corresponding type rating, while non-complex aircraft and component authority are checked under CCAR66.5/20, and not all supervised maintenance is treated as requiring an independent licence to release.
The licence category, the type ratings and the release authority are set out in the maintenance regulations and the organisation's authorisation documents.

A maintenance release must be carried out within the licence category and the type ratings; the licence privileges must not be exercised when the physiological condition is unsuitable (such as intoxication or illness); and work that does not meet the standard must not be released.
A defect or unairworthy condition must be reported promptly as required, and must not be concealed or released unilaterally because of schedule pressure.

A record applies only to the aircraft, component and job card it belongs to; a single inspection or a single measurement result must not be extrapolated into an airworthiness conclusion for a whole aircraft or for similar components, and a system prompt must not be treated as a basis for release.

Before starting, check at least six things: the licence and type ratings (category, engine category, complex-aircraft types); the employer type (airline, maintenance organisation MRO, manufacturer or general aviation); the scope of work (heavy check, line maintenance, component repair or avionics); the tooling and manual conditions (special tools, non-destructive testing equipment and the manual version); the duty pattern and work environment (shift work, apron and hangar, noise and temperature); and the training and authorisation path.
Look at the licence category and the type ratings, not at the job title.
Licence and type ratings: the aeroplane or rotorcraft category, the engine category, and whether the type rating for the complex aircraft being maintained is within its validity period.
Maintenance scope and authorisation systems differ between employers and must be checked against the specific organisation.
Employer type: airline engineering, an independent maintenance organisation (MRO), a manufacturer or general aviation; the work rhythm of line maintenance and of a deep heavy check differs greatly.
The scope of work determines the qualifications and tooling conditions required.
Scope of work: line maintenance, heavy check, component repair or avionics; and whether it involves non-destructive testing, engine removal and installation, or structural repair.
Special tools and the manual version are preconditions for being able to do the job.
Tools and manuals: whether the organisation provides special tools, non-destructive testing equipment and controlled manuals, and whether the manual version is current and valid.
Apron and hangar work places continuous demands on physical effort and protection.
Duty pattern and environment: whether there is shift and night work, exposure to high and low temperatures and noise on the apron, protective equipment and occupational-health arrangements.
The training and authorisation path affects long-term earnings and promotion.
Training and authorisation: whether the organisation provides type training and release authorisation, whether the licence category can be extended or type ratings added, and the promotion path.

paragraphs: A risk list cannot replace the airworthiness authority's maintenance regulations, the organisation's maintenance management manual and its working procedures; matters involving release standards, the execution of airworthiness directives and defect reporting must be carried out to the manual and the authority, and anything unclear should be confirmed by the quality department and the airworthiness management department. This page is not a legal or safety-policy opinion.

Four kinds of risk are most worth judging in advance: first, work and airworthiness risk (skipping the manual and the inspection points, a false measurement or torque record, a misjudged or missed non-destructive test); second, authority risk (carrying out maintenance and release beyond the licence category or the type ratings); third, parts and records risk (using an unapproved part, or an untrue or untraceable record); and fourth, occupational-health risk (exposure to noise, contaminants and high and low temperatures, and repetitive strain). The risk varies with the scope of work: line maintenance is closer to time pressure and the release judgement, while a deep heavy check is closer to workmanship quality and record completeness.

Evidence scope: O*NET 49-3011.00 provides the tasks and the work context (76% are exposed to noise every day, 77% consider precision or accuracy extremely important, 75% continuously handle tools with their hands); the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook provides the wages, employment and entry requirements; and the Rules on the Administration of Licences for Civil Aircraft Maintenance Personnel provide the mainland China licence categories, type ratings, release authority and defect-reporting duty. The risk list is an editorial summary and contains no probability of occurrence.

entries.answer: This occupation carries out maintenance and inspection under the continuing airworthiness documents and releases within the authority granted; flight operations are the pilot's responsibility; the repair plan and the release standard are set by the continuing airworthiness documents and the civil aviation authority; airworthiness oversight rests with the civil aviation authority; and aircraft design and airworthiness certification belong to another system and cannot be converted into this occupation's qualification or vice versa.
